findings.title: Require manage scope for global group mutations
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE, so an administrator granted only view access to all groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses that check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. This gives a read-only administrator write access to the group hierarchy. Check only MANAGE here and add a negative test that an all-groups VIEW permission cannot create or move groups.

findings.title: Resolve actual group IDs when building the user-search filter
findings.body: groupResource.getId() is an authorization resource ID, not a GroupModel ID: the schema creates a separate authorization resource with the model ID as its name. Passing this ID to hasPermission() makes its findByName() lookup miss, and returning it makes UsersResource filter membership using nonexistent group IDs. In particular, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission grants evaluation of the synthetic Groups resource, whose authorization ID is then used as the membership filter, causing user searches to return no members. Resolve concrete resources to model group IDs and expand the all-groups resource to actual groups instead of returning its ID. Cover both individual-group and all-groups member permissions in search/count tests.
